title: Non-blocking follow-ups from frontend-ibkr-status-indicator PR #244 review
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #244 (frontend-ibkr-status-indicator), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges. All static analysis (ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc), backend+frontend coverage (backend 99.95%, frontend 99.72%/99.19%/99.72%/99.79%, all-new-files 100%), the persisted e2e suite (18/18 passing, including the app-shell's new GET /api/ibkr/status call on every page), and a live browser walkthrough of all four gateway states plus a simulated transport failure passed cleanly -- these are refinements, not defects that block the accept.

checklist.step: Once `useIbkrStatus`'s initial fetch has succeeded at least once, a *later* background poll failure (the app's own backend genuinely going unreachable, not the IBKR gateway itself) does not flip `IbkrStatusIndicator` to the 'IBKR: Unknown' chip -- it keeps rendering the last successful state indefinitely. Root cause: TanStack Query keeps the previous `data` populated across a failed background refetch (its own default/documented behavior), and `IbkrStatusIndicator`'s check order (`if (!statusQuery.data) { if (statusQuery.isError) ... }`) only ever reaches the transport-failure branch when `data` is absent, so a stale-but-present `data` value short-circuits past `isError` becoming true. Verified directly with a vitest reproduction (fake timers: seed a successful 'available' response, let it render, then flip the MSW handler to `HttpResponse.error()` and advance 31s past the 30s `refetchInterval`) -- the badge kept reading 'IBKR: Connected' the whole time, with no 'ibkr-status-indicator-unknown' test id ever appearing. This contradicts this task's own 4th `decisions` entry, which claims a genuine transport failure is 'never folded into' one of the real gateway states -- in practice it can be silently masked by whatever state was last successfully fetched. Judged non-blocking rather than a review-blocker because the scenario requires this app's own backend to have died completely after at least one successful IBKR-status read, at which point every other page (Dashboard/Portfolio/Watchlist) already surfaces its own loud 'Something went wrong' error state from its own failed query -- so the practical user-facing risk of a stale IBKR chip specifically is low, but the gap is real and worth closing (e.g. render the transport-failure chip whenever `statusQuery.isError` is true regardless of stale `data`, or explicitly document this as an accepted limitation in the decision record instead of an unqualified claim).

Neither `IbkrStatusIndicator`'s loading spinner nor its rendered chip (via `IbkrStatusBadge` or the transport-failure 'Unknown' chip) is wrapped in an `aria-live`/`role="status"` region. Because this indicator is mounted once in `AppShell`'s app bar for the whole session and polls in the background every 30s with no user action, a screen-reader user who isn't currently focused on/near the app bar gets no announcement at all when the gateway's connectivity silently changes (e.g. it goes from 'Connected' to 'Gateway down' between polls) -- they'd have to re-visit the app bar to discover the change. `RiskPanel.tsx`'s `role="status"` box (for its own 'no risk data available for X' banner) is the closest existing precedent in this codebase for a similar case, though that one is triggered by a page-scoped data condition rather than a background poll. Worth adding a live region (or accepting and recording this as a deliberate scope cut, since no other status indicator in this codebase currently polls silently in the background either).
